1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.

## Type traps (strict `tsc` errors agents hit on a first draft)

| Error | Cause | Fix |

| `TS18048: 'app.camera' is possibly 'undefined'` | `app.camera` is an optional app extension. | Move the camera with `app.camera?.setPose(...)`, or declare it in the scene (`camera.orbit(...)`, `camera.perspective(...)`) and use `interactions.orbit` for user control. |
| `TS2339: Property 'translate' does not exist on type 'AuraNodeBuilder<...>'` | `translate` is on the live runtime handle (`app.nodes.require("name")`), not on the builders (`primitives.box(...)`). | On a builder use `.position(x, y, z)` or `.position([x, y, z])` (the array form needs 4.2.0 or later; on 4.1.3 and earlier pass three numbers). After mounting, move it with the handle's `translate` or `setPosition`. |

#1 [docs/agents/effects-and-scene-kits.md :: Contact shadows (screen-space mask)] score 9.7
### Contact shadows (screen-space mask)

`effects.contactShadows` builds a screen-space mask from scene depth and the sun direction, and forward lighting multiplies it into the visibility of the shadow-casting directional light (an absent mask is exactly 1.0). It is not the ambient-occlusion pass; the 4.5.0-prep lowering to SSAO is gone. Receipt `evidence/receipts/effects-contact-shadows/<version>.json` (software WebGL2, 600x400): with the subject outside the shadow map the near-base floor darkens by about 25 luma (48% of that region changes) and the far floor is unchanged; where the shadow map already shadows the receiver the mask adds little (0.08% of the frame changes, about 0.4 luma near the base), so do not expect a second shadow there.

Limits, all measured or asserted in the receipt and `tests/unit/rendering/contact-shadow-mask.test.ts`:

- It needs a directional light with `shadow: true`, and a shadow map only exists when at least one node has `castShadow: true`. With a spot or point light only, or none, nothing renders, `app.diagnostics().shadows.contactShadows.unavailable` says why (`no-shadow-casting-directional-light`) and one warning is logged; the on and off frames are pixel-identical.
- The nine textured-PBR glTF extension variants (clearcoat, transmission and similar) do not sample the mask.
